paragraphs: Dynex Capital, Inc. is a real estate investment trust ("REIT") structured to deliver dividends to shareholders supported by long term returns from investments in mortgage assets backed by U.S. housing and commercial real estate. Our common and preferred stocks trade on the New York Stock Exchange ("NYSE") under the ticker symbols "DX" and "DXPRC", respectively.

We are internally managed and invest primarily in residential and commercial mortgage-backed securities ("RMBS" and "CMBS", respectively), which are backed by residential and commercial mortgage loans, and which are Agency securities guaranteed by U.S. government-sponsored enterprises ("GSEs"). We may invest opportunistically in other mortgage-related assets consistent with our objectives. We actively manage interest rate, prepayment, spread, liquidity, and counterparty risks. The Dynex approach emphasizes risk management and disciplined capital allocation designed to preserve book value and support dividends across market cycles.

We operate to qualify as a REIT and to distribute at least 90% of our taxable income. We also seek to maintain exclusion from registration under the Investment Company Act of 1940 (the "1940 Act"). Please refer to "Operating and Regulatory Structure" within this Item 1, "Business" and Item 1A, "Risk Factors" of Part I of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for additional information.

Our business is subject to risks and uncertainties, including changes in interest rates and the yield curve, mortgage prepayments, market volatility and spread movements, financing conditions, counterparty performance, and regulatory and macroeconomic developments. Please refer to Item 1A, "Risk Factors," within this Part I as well as Part II, Item 7, "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations," and Item 7A, "Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk," of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for additional discussions of factors that have the potential to impact our results of operations and financial condition.

Our investment strategy and the allocation of our capital to a particular sector or investment is driven by a "top-down" framework that focuses on the risk management, scenario analysis, and expected risk-adjusted returns of any investment. Key aspects of this framework include the following:
•understanding macroeconomic factors, global monetary and fiscal policies, and variable outcomes;
•understanding the regulatory environment, competition for assets, and terms and availability of financing;
•investment analysis, including understanding absolute returns, relative and risk-adjusted returns, and supply/demand metrics in various mortgage asset classes;
•financing and hedging analysis, including sensitivity analysis on credit, interest rate volatility, liquidity, and market value risk; and
•managing performance and inherent portfolio risks, including but not limited to interest rate, credit, prepayment, and liquidity risks.

In allocating our capital and executing our strategy, we seek to balance the risks of owning specific types of investments with the earnings opportunity on the investment. Though the majority of our investment portfolio is currently in fixed-rate Agency RMBS, we may allocate capital from time to time to a variety of other investments, including adjustable-rate Agency RMBS, fixed-rate Agency CMBS, investment grade and unrated non-Agency RMBS and CMBS, Agency and non-Agency CMBS IO, and residual interests in securitized mortgage loans. Our investments in non-Agency MBS are generally higher quality senior or mezzanine classes (typically rated 'A' or better by one or more of the nationally recognized statistical rating organizations) because they are typically more liquid (i.e., they are more easily converted into cash either through sales or pledges as collateral for repurchase agreement borrowings) and have less exposure to credit losses than lower-rated non-Agency MBS. We regularly review our existing operations to determine whether our investment strategy or business model should change, including through capital reallocation, changing our targeted investments as well as hedging instruments and shifting our risk position.

From time to time, we analyze and evaluate potential business opportunities that we identify or are presented to us, including possible partnerships, mergers, acquisitions, or divestiture transactions that might maximize value for our shareholders. Pursuing such an opportunity or transaction could require us to issue additional equity or debt securities.

RMBS. As of December 31, 2025, the majority of our investments were Agency-issued pass-through RMBS collateralized primarily by pools of fixed-rate single-family mortgage loans. Monthly payments of principal and interest made by the individual borrowers on the mortgage loans underlying the pools are "passed through" to the security holders after deducting GSE or U.S. government agency guarantee and servicing fees. Mortgage pass-through certificates generally distribute cash flows from the underlying collateral on a pro-rata basis among the security holders. Security holders also receive guarantor advances of principal and interest for delinquent loans in the mortgage pools.

We also purchase to-be-announced securities ("TBAs" or "TBA securities") as a means of investing in non-specified fixed-rate Agency RMBS, and from time to time, we may also sell TBA securities to economically hedge our book value exposure to Agency RMBS. A TBA security is a forward contract ("TBA contract") for the purchase ("long position") or sale ("short position") of a fixed-rate Agency MBS at a predetermined price with certain principal and interest terms and certain types of collateral. The actual Agency securities to be delivered are not identified until approximately two days before the settlement date. We hold long and short positions in TBA securities by executing a series of transactions, commonly referred to as "dollar roll" transactions, which effectively delay the settlement of a forward purchase (or sale) of a non-specified Agency RMBS by entering into an offsetting TBA position, net settling the paired-off positions in cash, and simultaneously entering into an identical TBA long (or short) position with a later settlement date. TBA securities purchased or sold for a forward settlement date are generally priced at a discount relative to TBA securities settling in the current month because the current month settlement will receive a coupon sooner than the TBA settling in a forward month. This price difference, often referred to as "drop income," represents the economic equivalent of net interest income (interest income less implied financing cost) on the underlying Agency security from the trade date to the settlement date. We account for all TBAs (whether net long or net short positions, or collectively "TBA dollar roll positions") as derivative instruments because we cannot assert that it is probable at inception and throughout the term of an individual TBA transaction that its settlement will result in physical delivery of the underlying Agency RMBS, or that the individual TBA transaction will settle in the shortest period possible.

headings: Changes in market spreads may negatively impact the market value and profitability of our investment portfolio.
Interest rate fluctuations could negatively impact our financing costs, the market value of our investments, dividends, liquidity, and the market price of our stock.
Changes in the Federal Reserve, government agency, or other government related entity participation in the Agency mortgage market may impact the market value and return on our investments.

Changes in prepayment rates on the mortgage loans underlying our investments may subject us to reinvestment risk and adversely affect our interest income, the market value of our investments, and our liquidity.
It could be uneconomical to roll our TBA contracts or we may be unable to meet margin calls on our TBA contracts, which would have a negative impact on our liquidity.
Provisions requiring yield maintenance charges, prepayment penalties, defeasance, or lockouts in CMBS IO securities may not be enforceable.
Our use of hedging strategies to mitigate our interest rate risk may not be effective and may adversely affect our net income, liquidity, and book value per common share.

Clearing facilities or exchanges may increase the margin requirements we are required to post when entering into derivative instruments, which may negatively impact our ability to hedge and our liquidity.
We may incur significant losses if we, or one or more of our third-party lenders, default on a repurchase agreement or file for bankruptcy.
The models we use to make purchases and risk management decisions for our portfolio may be inaccurate or incomplete, which could materially and adversely affect our cash flows.
If we fail to conduct our operations properly, we may not qualify for exemption under the 1940 Act, which may reduce our flexibility and limit our ability to pursue certain opportunities.
We may be subject to adverse legislative or regulatory tax changes that could increase our tax liability, reduce our operating flexibility, or reduce the market price of our securities.
Dividends payable by REITs do not qualify for the reduced tax rates available for some dividends.
Uncertainty exists with respect to the treatment of our TBAs for purposes of the REIT asset and income tests.
Our ability to qualify as a REIT could be adversely affected if the IRS disagrees with our treatment of repurchase agreement transactions as financing of the investments we pledge as collateral.
Even if we remain qualified as a REIT, we may face other tax liabilities that reduce our cash flow and our profitability.
Future issuances of equity securities may dilute your percentage ownership in us and may also negatively affect the market price of our common stock.

paragraphs: The following is a discussion of the risk factors we believe are material to our business. These are factors that, individually or in the aggregate, we think could cause our actual results to differ significantly from anticipated or historical results. In addition to understanding the key risks described below, investors should understand that it is not possible to predict or identify all risk factors. Consequently, the following is not a complete discussion of all potential risks or uncertainties facing our business.
RISKS RELATED TO OUR INVESTMENT ACTIVITIES

Changes in market spreads represent the market's valuation of the perceived riskiness of assets relative to risk-free rates. Market spreads change based on factors specific to a particular security, such as prepayment performance or credit performance, and other factors, including, but not limited to, macroeconomic and systemic changes, market psychology, market liquidity, and Federal Reserve monetary policies. When spreads widen, the market value of our investments will decline because market participants typically require additional yield to hold

riskier assets. Spread levels also impact income over the longer term. When market spreads tighten, we pay a higher premium for new investments, which lowers the yield we expect to earn on our future investment portfolio.

Interest rate fluctuations impact us in multiple ways. During periods of rising rates, particularly interest rate increases that occur with increases to the targeted U.S. Federal Funds Rate ("Federal Funds Rate"), we may experience a decline in our net interest income because interest rates paid on our borrowings may increase faster than interest rates earned on our investments. While the Federal Reserve continued to reduce the targeted Federal Funds Rate in 2025, future reductions are not certain, and there can be no assurance that the Federal Reserve will not make upwards adjustments to the Federal Funds Rate in the future. Any increases in the Federal Funds Rate, and market anticipation of the same, are likely to cause our borrowing costs to increase, negatively impacting our net interest income, common stock dividends, market price of our stock, and book value per common share.

Interest rate increases may also negatively affect the market value of our securities, and if we do not adequately hedge against such increases, we will experience declines in comprehensive income, book value per common share, and liquidity. Since our investment portfolio consists substantially of fixed rate instruments, rising interest rates will reduce the market value of our MBS as market participants will in turn demand higher yielding assets. Reductions in the market value of our MBS typically result in margin calls from our lenders, which impacts our liquidity. Furthermore, an increasing interest rate environment may expose us to extension risk as prepayments on the loans underlying our MBS are likely to decline, which may reduce our ability to reinvest into higher yielding assets.

paragraphs: Our 2025 results directly reflected our ability to capitalize on this favorable environment while maintaining disciplined risk management. For the year ended December 31, 2025, our total economic return ("TER") of $2.75 per common share, or 21.6% of beginning book value, was comprised of an increase in book value of $0.75 per common share and dividends declared of $2.00 per common share. The increase in our book value was predominantly driven by asset appreciation due to tighter spreads between our asset yields and the yields on our interest rate swaps and Treasury futures.The Company's results for 2025 also benefited from higher net interest income due to its purchases of Agency RMBS and CMBS throughout the year at higher yield levels than 2024 while related repurchase agreement financing costs fell following three U.S. Federal Funds rate cuts in 2025. Our increase in the use of SOFR-based interest rate swaps in 2025 added to economic net interest income.

Our total equity and market capitalization as of December 31, 2025 more than doubled since December 31, 2024 primarily because we raised over $1.2 billion through the issuance of over 90 million shares of common stock pursuant to our ATM program. We deployed the majority of this capital into opportunities in the Agency MBS market, while also strengthening our organization with refreshed leadership, a new independent auditor, and an expanded office footprint.

For our shareholders, 2025 delivered a 29.4% total return including dividends and share price appreciation. Over this decade through December 31, 2025, Dynex shareholders have experienced a 67% cumulative total return, or approximately 9% annualized with dividends reinvested.

paragraphs: Dynex Capital, Inc. 為一間不動產投資信託（"REIT"），其結構旨在透過投資於美國住宅及商業不動產抵押資產所產生的長期回報，向股東發放股息。本公司普通股與優先股於紐約證券交易所（"NYSE"）交易，代碼分別為 "DX" 與 "DXPRC"。
本公司為內部管理，主要投資於住宅及商業抵押-backed 債券（"RMBS" 及 "CMBS"），這些債券由住宅及商業抵押貸款支持，且為美國政府支持企業（"GSEs"）擔保的機構債券。本公司可能根據投資目標，有機會性地投資於其他與抵押相關的資產。本公司積極管理利率、預付、利差、流動性及交易對手風險。Dynex 的策略強調風險管理及嚴謹的資本配置，旨在維持帳面價值並支持股息，不受市場週期影響。
本公司運作目標為符合 REIT 的條件，並至少分派 90% 的應稅所得。本公司亦致力於維持不註冊於 1940 年投資公司法（"1940 Act"）。請參閱本 10-K 申報書第一部分「業務」項目 1 中的「運作與法規結構」，以及第一部分項目 1A「風險因素」，以取得更多資訊。
本公司業務面臨風險與不確定性，包括利率與收益率曲線的變動、抵押貸款預付、市場波動與利差變動、融資條件、交易對手錶現，以及法規與總體經濟發展。請參閱本部分第一部分項目 1A「風險因素」，以及第二部分項目 7「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析」，以及項目 7A「市場風險之量化與質化揭露」，以取得更多有關可能影響本公司營運成果與財務狀況的相關因素之討論。
本公司投資策略與資本配置至特定產業或投資的決定，係基於一項「自上而下」的架構，該架構著重於任何投資之風險管理、情境分析及預期風險調整後回報。此架構的關鍵方面包括以下內容：
•瞭解並評估總體經濟因素、全球貨幣與財政政策及變動結果；
•瞭解並評估法規環境、資產競爭情形及融資條款與可得性；
•投資分析，包括瞭解並評估絕對回報、相對與風險調整後回報，以及各類抵押資產之供需指標；
•財務籌資與避險分析，包括對信貸、利率波動、流動性及市場價值風險的敏感度分析；以及
•管理績效與內在投資組合風險，包括但不限於利率、信貸、預付款及流動性風險。

在配置我們的資本並執行我們的策略時，我們會權衡持有特定類型投資的風險與該投資的獲利機會。儘管目前我們的投資組合主要為固定利率的機構發行房貸支持證券（Agency RMBS），我們有時會將資本配置至其他種類的投資，包括浮動利率的機構發行房貸支持證券（Agency RMBS）、固定利率的機構發行商業抵押貸款支持證券（Agency CMBS）、投資等級及未評級的非機構發行房貸支持證券（RMBS）與商業抵押貸款支持證券（CMBS）、機構發行與非機構發行商業抵押貸款支持證券（CMBS）的利息權（IO），以及抵押貸款證券化的殘餘權益。我們對非機構發行房貸支持證券（MBS）的投資通常為較高品質的優先級或次級級別（通常由一個或多個 nationally recognized statistical rating organizations 評為 'A' 或以上），因為這些證券通常較具流動性（即較容易透過銷售或作為追繳協議借款的擔保品轉換為現金），且對信用損失的暴露較低於評級較低的非機構發行房貸支持證券（MBS）。我們會定期檢視現有業務運作，以判斷是否應調整投資策略或商業模式，包括透過資本重新配置、改變目標投資以及避險工具，並調整風險敞口。
有時，我們會分析與評估我們所識別或被提出的潛在商業機會，包括可能的合作夥伴關係、合併、收購或資產處分交易，以最大化對股東的價值。追求這樣的機會或交易可能需要我們發行額外的普通股或債務證券。

房貸支持證券（RMBS）。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的投資主要為機構發行的過手式房貸支持證券（Agency-issued pass-through RMBS），這些證券主要由固定利率的單戶房貸貸款池所擔保。個別借款人對房貸貸款所支付的本金與利息，會在扣除 GSE 或美國政府機構擔保與服務費用後，「過手」至證券持有人。房貸過手證券通常會根據基礎資產的狀況，按比例分配現金流至證券持有人。證券持有人也會收到擔保人對逾期貸款的本金與利息預付金。

我們也會透過購入待宣佈證券（"TBAs" 或 "TBA 證券"）來投資非特定的固定利率機構發行房貸支持證券（Agency RMBS），有時我們也會出售 TBA 證券，以經濟上避險我們對機構發行房貸支持證券（Agency RMBS）的帳面價值風險。TBA 證券是一種遠期合約（"TBA 合約"），用以購買（"長頭寸"）或出售（"短頭寸"）固定利率的機構發行房貸支持證券（MBS），以預定價格進行交易，並具備特定的本金與利息條件及特定類型的擔保品。實際交付的機構發行證券在結算日約兩天前才會確定。我們透過執行一系列交易（通常稱為 "美元滾" 交易）來持有長頭寸與短頭寸的 TBA 證券，這些交易有效地延遲了非特定機構發行房貸支持證券（Agency RMBS）遠期買入（或賣出）的結算，透過建立一個對沖的 TBA 側位，以現金結算配對的頭寸，並同時建立一個相同類型的 TBA 長頭寸（或短頭寸）且結算日較晚的交易。為遠期結算日購入或售出的 TBA 證券，通常會以較低價格交易，相較於當月結算的 TBA 證券，因為當月結算的證券會較早收到票息。這種價格差異，通常稱為 "落差收入"，代表從交易日到結算日，對應基礎機構發行證券的淨利息收入（利息收入減去隱含的融資成本）的經濟價值。我們將所有 TBA（無論為淨長頭寸或淨短頭寸，或合併為 "TBA 美元滾" 側位）視為衍生工具，因為我們無法在個別 TBA 交易的起始時點及整個合約期間內，合理預期其結算會導致基礎機構發行房貸支持證券（MBS）的實際交付，或個別 TBA 交易會在最短時間內結算。

paragraphs: 我們 2025 年的營運成果直接反映本公司在有利環境中把握機會的能力，同時維持嚴謹的風險管理。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日為止，本公司每股普通股總經濟回報（"TER"）為 2.75 美元，或為期初帳面價值的 21.6%，包含每股普通股帳面價值增加 0.75 美元及每股普通股宣佈的股息 2.00 美元。本公司帳面價值的增加主要來自資產價值因資產收益率與利率期貨收益率間的利差收窄而產生的升值。本公司 2025 年的營運成果亦受益於淨利息收入增加，因本公司於 2025 年全年以高於 2024 年的收益率購入 Agency RMBS 及 CMBS，同時因美國聯邦基金利率在 2025 年下降三次，相關回購協議融資成本降低。本公司於 2025 年增加使用基於 SOFR 的利率期貨，進一步提高經濟淨利息收入。
本公司總資本及市場總值於2025年12月31日較2024年12月31日成長逾一倍，主要係因本公司透過ATM方案發行逾90百萬股普通股，籌得逾1.2十億美元。本公司將此資金的大多數投入Agency MBS市場的機會，同時也透過更新領導階層、聘請新的獨立會計師及擴充辦公據點來強化組織。
對股東而言，2025 年實現總回報率為 29.4%，包含股息與股價升值。自 2015 年 12 月 31 日至 2025 年 12 月 31 日為止，Dynex 股東累計總回報率為 67%，或年化約 9%（包含再投資的股息）。

headings: 市場 spreads 的變動可能對我們投資組合的市場價值及獲利能力產生負面影響。
利率波動可能對我們的融資成本、投資的市場價值、股息、流動性以及股票市場價格產生負面影響。
聯邦儲備委員會、政府機構或其他與政府相關機構參與機構房貸市場的程度變動，可能影響我們投資的市場價值及回報。
機構房貸貸款預付款率的變動可能使我們面臨再投資風險，並對我們的利息收入、投資的市場價值及流動性產生負面影響。
滾動我們的 TBA 合約可能不經濟，或我們可能無法滿足 TBA 合約的擔保金要求，這將對我們的流動性產生負面影響。
要求收益率維持費用、預付款罰款、贖回或鎖定期的 CMBS IO 證券條款可能無法執行。
我們使用避險策略來降低利率風險，可能無法達到預期效果，並對我們的淨收入、流動性及每股帳面價值產生負面影響。
結算機構或交易所可能提高我們在進行衍生工具交易時需繳納的擔保金要求，這可能對我們的避險能力及流動性產生負面影響。
我們若未能履行買回協議或與第三方貸款人一同申請破產，可能會產生重大虧損。
我們用以進行投資組合購入及風險管理決策的模型可能不準確或不完整，這可能會對我們的現金流造成重大且不利的影響。
若我們未能妥善進行營運，可能會無法符合1940年法案的豁免條件，這可能會降低我們的靈活性，並限制我們追求某些機會的能力。
我們可能面臨不利的立法或監管稅務變動，這可能會增加我們的稅務負擔、降低我們的營運靈活性，或降低我們證券的市場價格。
REITs所支付的股息不符合某些股息可適用的減稅率。
關於我們的TBAs在REIT資產與收入測試中的處理方式，存在不確定性。
若國稅局不同意我們將買回協議交易視為擔保投資的融資方式，可能會影響我們符合REIT資格的條件。
即使我們持續符合REIT資格，仍可能面臨其他稅務負擔，這會降低我們的現金流與獲利能力。
未來發行 equity securities 可能稀釋您在我們公司的持股比例，也可能對我們普通股的市場價格產生負面影響。

paragraphs: 以下為我們認為對我們業務具重大影響之風險因素之討論。這些因素，個別或整體而言，我們認為可能會導致我們實際結果與預期或歷史結果產生顯著差異。除了瞭解下列所說明之關鍵風險外，投資人應瞭解無法預測或識別所有風險因素。因此，以下並非對我們業務所有潛在風險或不確定性之完整討論。
與我們投資活動相關之風險
市場利差之變動反映市場對資產風險性相對於無風險利率之評估。市場利差會根據特定證券之因素，例如預付款表現或信用表現，以及其他因素，包括但不限於總體經濟與系統性變動、市場心理、市場流動性及美國聯邦儲備委員會之貨幣政策而變化。當利差擴大時，我們投資之市場價值將下降，因為市場參與者通常需要更高的報酬率以持有較高風險之資產。
利差水平也會影響長期之收入。當市場利差收窄時，我們對新投資之買價將提高，這會降低我們預期在未來投資組閤中所獲得之報酬率。

利率波動會以多種方式影響我們。在利率上漲期間，特別是在美國聯邦基金利率（"聯邦基金利率"）上調之情況下，我們可能因所支付之借款利率上升速度高於所賺取之投資利率，而導致淨利息收入下降。雖然美國聯邦儲備委員會在2025年持續降低目標聯邦基金利率，但未來是否進一步降低尚不確定，且無法保證美國聯邦儲備委員會不會在未來對聯邦基金利率進行上調。任何聯邦基金利率上調，以及市場對此之預期，都可能導致我們之借款成本上升，進而對我們之淨利息收入、普通股股息、股票市場價格及每股帳面價值造成負面影響。

利率上漲也可能對我們之證券市場價值產生負面影響，若我們未能充分對此進行避險，我們將會經歷綜合收入、每股帳面價值及流動性之下降。由於我們之投資組合主要由固定利率工具組成，利率上漲將降低我們之MBS（房貸支持證券）之市場價值，因為市場參與者將要求更高的報酬率之資產。我們之MBS市場價值之降低通常會導致我們之貸款人提出追加保證金之要求，進而影響我們之流動性。此外，在利率上漲之環境下，我們可能面臨延長風險，因為我們之MBS所基礎之貸款之預付款率可能下降，這可能會降低我們重新投資至更高報酬率資產之能力。
